title: App Builder Site Plan
description: What pages exist, why each deserves to exist separately, and what sequence of content belongs on it — decided from approved truth before any presentation choice is made. This is the artifact `config/agent-roles.json` has called InformationArchitectureSpec since the roles were written, with schema null and status planned, while the decision it names was actually taken by a literal array keyed on project type: marketing-site meant Home, Services, About, Contact, and a page's purpose was then inferred by matching a regular expression against its own name. A plan carries no target route count, no target section count and no shape quota. Deciding on less structure is a valid outcome and `omitted` is where that decision is recorded, because a planner that can only ever add is a template with a variable in it.

thesis.description: One sentence saying what this site is for. Not a tagline: the sentence a route has to be consistent with to earn its place.

job.description: What this person is trying to get done. Not who they are.

routes.description: One route is a legitimate plan. So is eight. Neither is a target.

omitted.description: Structure the plan considered and declined, with the reason. Required — not optional — because 'we chose less' is otherwise invisible and indistinguishable from 'we did not think of it'. A thin-truth business should produce entries here rather than routes filled with generic copy.

foldedInto.description: The route that carries this truth instead, or null when the truth is too thin to carry anywhere.

purpose.description: What this page is for, in the plan's own words.

entryQuestion.description: What a visitor arrives at this page asking. A page whose question is answered by another page does not need to exist.

existsBecause.description: Why this deserves to be a page rather than a section of one. Validated against a list of justifications that say nothing — 'provides useful information', 'builds trust', 'showcases services' — because those are the sentences a generator reaches for when it has no reason.

factRefs.description: Approved truth this route may draw on. Every id must resolve in the KnowledgePack. The planner may reorganise approved knowledge and may not invent any.

exitAction.description: What the visitor can do from here, or null where the honest answer is that this page only informs.

narrative.description: Ordered. What must be established before what.

job.description: What this section does in this page's narrative. Unique within a route: two sections doing the same job are one section rendered twice.

binds.description: The family of approved truth this section renders — a fact about the business, never a component name. Composition maps it to a presentation; the plan does not choose one.

covers.description: Whether this section carries its truth in full, or shows enough of it to send a visitor to the route that does. A semantic distinction, not a presentational one: it is the difference between a page that answers a question and a page that routes it. Without it a home page either repeats every other page or has nothing to route with, which are the two failure modes this capability was built to separate.

establishes.description: What a reader knows after this section that they did not before.

requires.description: Jobs that must come earlier in this route. Backwards only — a narrative that depends on something later is not an order.
